source.thread: A prophet writes the death of a man he never met 700 years early - wounded for our transgressions - and when a traveller asks who it is, the New Testament answers by name: Jesus
source.hook_line: # Isaiah 53 — The Suffering Servant (LONG-FORM PILOT) - **Series root:** Jesus in the Old Testament (Awakeden) — long-form deep-dive - **Passage:** Isaiah 52:13
source.spoken_script: # Isaiah 53 — The Suffering Servant (LONG-FORM PILOT) - **Series root:** Jesus in the Old Testament (Awakeden) — long-form deep-dive - **Passage:** Isaiah 52:13 – 53:12 (the full fourth Servant Song) - **Format:** 16:9, ~6–7 min, reverent documentary pace - **Spine:** Deep-Dive Seven-Movement (Report → Scandal → Exchange → Silent Lamb + Objection → Fulfilment → Will of the LORD → Arm of the LORD) - **Voices:** `narrator` throughout · `the_LORD` for "Behold, my servant" · `eunuch` for the Acts 8 question · KJV verbatim for all quoted Scripture - **Doctrine:** penal substitution, sinless Servant, real resurrection hint, grace-anchored landing — evangelical, non-negotiable - **Status:** v3 — KJV verbatim RE-LOCK (2026-06-04). The enforced cursor+panel independent review (4/5 REVISE) caught an Acts 8:35 elision the engine pass had missed. Fixed: Acts 8:35 (now full verbatim "opened his mouth, and…"), Isaiah 53:10–11 (continuous verbatim, no interior ellipsis), 49:3 (extended to the full clause: "Thou art my servant, O Israel, in whom I will be glorified."), 53:3 (trailing ellipsis, no invented period), "pierced"→"wounded" (M7, matches KJV 53:5), and consistent leading/trailing ellipsis marking on all excerpted quotes. Affected audio turns re-rendered + verified by ASR. Two enforced panel passes confirmed KJV WORDS clean across all 17 spans (claude PASS). Then applied 4 convergent EDITORIAL fixes the panel surfaced (user-approved): M1 "the rich man in his death" (not "own it" — drops the fulfilment over-reach); M6 resurrection kept hint-only (dropped "risen Servant" / "It worked"); M7 "taken away" (not "paid in full" — removes transaction framing from the landing, per the locked grace rule); M7 "wounded for your transgressions, and bore them in your place" (not "so that you would not have to be"). Audio re-rendered again → 482.89s, ASR-verified (new wording in, flagged wording out). Prior: v2 external panel merge (2026-06-03). LOCKED. --- ## MOVEMENT 1 — THE REPORT *(~40s · cold open)* **[narrator]** Seven hundred years before a Roman nail was ever driven through a human wrist, a prophet in Jerusalem wrote down the death of a man he had never met. He described the wounds, the silence, the grave — and the rich man in his death. He even wrote down what the wounds were *for*. And then he asked the question that still hangs over the page: **[narrator — KJV, Isaiah 53:1]** "Who hath believed our report? and to whom is the arm of the LORD revealed?" **[narrator]** This is Isaiah fifty-three. Either it is the most astonishing accident in all of human literature — or someone standing outside of time was telling us, centuries early, exactly how God would save the world. --- ## MOVEMENT 2 — BEHOLD MY SERVANT *(~50s · the scandal)* **[narrator]** It opens with God Himself pointing. **[the_LORD — KJV, Isaiah 52:13]** "Behold, my servant shall deal prudently, he shall be exalted and extolled, and be very high." **[narrator]** You brace yourself for a conquering king. And then the picture breaks. **[narrator — KJV, Isaiah 52:14]** "…his visage was so marred more than any man, and his form more than the sons of men…" — **[narrator]** a face beaten past recognising. **[narrator — KJV, Isaiah 53:2-3]** "…he hath no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him. He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief…" **[narrator]** God's chosen Servant does not arrive in armour. He arrives in agony. The world looks at him — and looks away. The exalted one and the despised one are the same man. Hold those two together — that tension is the whole gospel in a single breath. --- ## MOVEMENT 3 — THE EXCHANGE *(~65s · the heart)* **[narrator]** Then comes the centre of the chapter — and every line is a transaction. **[narrator — KJV, Isaiah 53:4]** "Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows…" — **[narrator]** *our* griefs. Not his own. **[narrator — KJV, Isaiah 53:5]**

platforms.description:
Seven hundred years before a Roman nail was ever driven, a prophet in Jerusalem wrote down the death of a man he had never met (Isaiah 53).

"But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed" (Isaiah 53:5, KJV).

The wounds, the silence, the grave, the rich man in his death, and what the wounds were for. Then a traveller on a desert road asks the question the whole chapter waits for: of whom speaketh the prophet this? And the New Testament answers by name.

The report is true. Come to the One it names.

platforms.title: Isaiah 53: The Death Described 700 Years Before It Happened
platforms.description:
Seven hundred years before a Roman nail was ever driven, a prophet in Jerusalem wrote down the death of a man he had never met: the wounds, the silence, the grave, the rich man in his death, and what the wounds were for (Isaiah 52:13-53:12).

"But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed" (Isaiah 53:5, KJV).

This deep-dive walks the whole fourth Servant Song, movement by movement: the report no one believed; the Servant exalted and then marred more than any man; the exchange at the chapter's centre, where every line is a transaction; the lamb silent before her shearers; the honest question thoughtful Jewish readers raise, whether the Servant is Israel, taken seriously and answered from the text itself; the moment in Acts 8 when a traveller reading this very chapter asks, of whom speaketh the prophet this, and Philip, beginning at the same scripture, preaches unto him Jesus; the line heavier than all the wounds, that it pleased the LORD to bruise him; and the quiet turn toward morning, a grave that could not be the end of him.

The arm of the LORD is not a thing. It is a person, and he has your name in verse six: all we like sheep have gone astray. Already carried. Already taken away. You do not have to clean yourself up before you come.

The report is true. The arm of the LORD has a name. Have you believed the report?

redteam:
VERDICT: REVISE

- youtube_long (unmarked KJV fragments): the description weaves near-verbatim KJV into prose without quote marks - "of whom speaketh the prophet this" (Acts 8:34) and "all we like sheep have gone astray" (Isaiah 53:6). Both hug the KJV so closely they read as quotations. Fix: quote-mark both at the point of quotation - asks, "of whom speaketh the prophet this?" ... and: "All we like sheep have gone astray" (Isaiah 53:6). The Philip line ("beginning at the same scripture, preaches unto him Jesus") changes tense from Acts 8:35; either quote it exactly or loosen the paraphrase so it cannot be mistaken for the verse.
- Long-unit completeness: this kit must ship with CHAPTERS (the film's seven movements, timed) and a PINNED_COMMENT in youtube_long.md - the publish gate fails a long unit without them. They are not in this draft and must be authored before the pack is called done.
- KJV check: Isaiah 53:5 is verbatim as supplied on every platform that quotes it, marked and attributed, ref front-loaded. Instagram's partial quote is marked and labeled (Isaiah 53:5, KJV). PASS.
- Honesty: "700 years" matches the narration's own claim; the description promises exactly the film's seven movements including the Israel objection treated seriously; "Have you believed the report?" is the film's own closing line. No clickbait, no overclaim.
- Grace check: the landing ("Already carried. Already taken away. You do not have to clean yourself up before you come") is the film's own grace-anchored wording; no fear or gain-loss framing. PASS.
- Titles: chosen title is specific, honest, and collides with no sibling. PASS.
